notes.title: Patch #3 – Survivor Mode is Here!
notes.notes:
Hi everyone,

Patch #3 is live, and it’s our biggest update so far! This update brings bug fixes, polish, and quality-of-life improvements, but the real highlight is something many of you have asked for: a brand new game mode – Survivor Mode.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45097607/4ca914a04e351d6984a7bbdc5d8bff9d6137a15e.png"]
What is Survivor Mode?
Survivor Mode is all about jumping straight into the action. Instead of building up a base and slowly preparing for waves, you’ll be thrown right into the fight:

You start with a Mech at its lowest upgrades, armed only with the Katana sword.



Alien waves begin immediately and keep getting tougher with new enemy types and higher intensity.

There’s no base building here. Instead, you’ll need to clear alien nests to unlock upgrades and new weapons.

Survivor Mode also features exclusive Orbital Strike weapons that can’t be found anywhere else.

And if you manage to survive long enough… the final boss will appear. Beat it, and you’ve conquered the run.

This mode is designed for those of you who wanted a faster, more action-packed experience, while Classic Mode remains for players who love the more strategic, colony-building gameplay.
Other Updates in Patch #3
Bug fixes for stability and smoother play.

Quality-of-life improvements across the board.

UI, audio, and balance polish.
A Note from Me
I’m beyond excited to finally share Survivor Mode with you all. It’s been a long road getting here, and your feedback has been an essential part of shaping this game. If you’re enjoying it, please consider leaving a Steam review—it helps me out so much as a solo developer.

And of course, come join us on Discord to share your feedback, bug reports, and survivor stories. I can’t wait to hear what you think of the new mode!

See you out there,
Nima

notes.title: Patch #2 Release Notes - Full Controller Support + Smarter Enemies
notes.notes:
Full Controller Support + Smarter Enemies
Release Date: 2025-06-24

Patch #2 is here, and the main focus has been making Wave Defense: Trappist more accessible—especially for controller players and Steam Deck users. This update also includes improvements to enemy AI and balance tweaks to raise the challenge and keep battles engaging.

Controller Support

 Full support for PlayStation and Xbox controllers has been added.
 The entire game is now fully playable on Steam Deck.
 All menus, UI, and in-game systems have been updated to work seamlessly with controller input.

Enemy AI Improvements

 Enemies now react more intelligently when attacked, improving the flow and feel of combat.
 Behavior adjustments lead to more dynamic engagements, especially in mid- to late-game waves.
 Enemy Balance Tweaks
 Slight increases to enemy health across various types.

These changes are aimed at making combat more satisfying and a bit more challenging, especially for experienced players.

More improvements are in the works, and your feedback continues to shape every update. If you haven’t already, join us in the Discord to share your thoughts or report any issues. Thanks for playing!

notes.title: Patch #1 - Release Notes
notes.notes:
The first major patch is here! This update focuses on expanding gameplay with new upgrade systems, polishing existing features, improving UI and audio feedback, and fixing bugs based on community feedback.

We’re also incredibly excited to release the official soundtrack as a DLC, featuring music by world-renowned electronic producer Joel Mull. The music has been a core part of the game’s atmosphere from the start, and now you can enjoy it outside the game as well. Huge thanks to Joel for crafting such a powerful and immersive soundscape!

Thank you to everyone who’s played and supported the game since launch!

New Feature: Building Upgrade Station
The Building Upgrade Station is now active. You can spend Crystals mined during your runs to unlock permanent meta-upgrades that strengthen your colonies across future playthroughs.

New upgrades include:

 Alpha-7 Droid – A powerful new droid unit assembled at the Droid Factory.
 Shield Domes – Add protective shielding to your turrets.
 Improved Power Plants – Increased energy output for more efficient colonies.
 Enhanced Trading Outposts – Boost your resource management and economy.

Game Balance

 Reworked enemy scaling and resource pacing to make difficulty progression more consistent.
 Buffs and nerfs to select weapons, perks, and enemy waves for improved game flow and strategic variety.

UI & Quality of Life

 Updated menus and HUD for better readability and cleaner visuals.
 [Pause menu now correctly displays detailed information across all tabs, especially the Building tab.

Weapon Improvements

 All weapons have received an updated audio mix to ensure better in-game feedback and impact.
 

Building Polish

 Adjusted build sizes for the Droid Factory and Trading Outpost to improve placement.
 General polish pass on building visuals and construction feedback.

Bug Fixes

 Fixed an issue where the Building tab in the pause menu was not displaying correct values.
 Audio feedback updated for XP, Credit, and Crystal pickups.
 Fixed issue with Droid combat circle indicator not deactivating after deployment.

Thanks again for all your feedback, suggestions, and support! We’re already working on what’s next. If you haven’t yet, join the conversation over on the Discord and help shape the future of the game.

notes.title: First week after the release!
notes.notes:
Hey everyone,

The game is now officially released! It’s been a long road to get here, and seeing my first game out in the world is a huge moment. I’ve learned so much along the way, and I want to thank my friends and everyone at Caketown for all the help and support in getting the game across the finish line.

A special thank you also goes to electronic music legend Joel Mull, who composed the game’s original soundtrack. It adds so much atmosphere to the world, and I’m thrilled to announce that the soundtrack will be released as a DLC alongside the first post-launch patch on April 8th!

Building Upgrade Station
Activate the station to unlock meta-upgrades using Crystals mined during your runs. Upgrades include:

notes.title: How to Transfer Your Save File from the Demo to the Full Version
notes.notes:
If you’ve been playing the Wave Defense: Trappist demo and want to carry your progress —including your Mech paint jobs— over to the full game, follow these simple steps:
[olist]
 Install the Full Game on Steam – Make sure the main game is fully installed.
 Start a New Run in the full version. This will create the necessary save file.
 Before uninstalling the demo, confirm that your progress and custom Mech paint jobs appear in the full game.
 Once everything looks good, you can safely uninstall the demo version from Steam.
[/olist]
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45097607/cc49d2b2b73cfeda00d325dea01c2e5417642a93.png

By following these steps, you’ll ensure that all your progress and personalized Mech paint jobs carry over smoothly. If you need any help, feel free to ask in the Discord!

Join the Discord!

notes.title: Demo Patch #3
notes.notes:
Hello everyone! 

Rolling out a new update based on the feedback we’ve received from you. Your input has been instrumental in improving the game, so please keep it coming—either through the in-game feedback tool or by joining our Discord community! 

Main Focus: Optimization, Polish, and New Features

This update brings major optimizations, UI improvements, and some exciting new features to Wave Defense: Trappist! The goal has been to refine the game, make it more accessible to more players, and introduce new ways to personalize your Mech.

New Features & Changes

 Unlockable Mech Cosmetics – Level up your Mech in a run to unlock new visual gadgets that showcase your piloting skills. No gameplay impact—just bragging rights!
 New HUD UI – A redesigned HUD that provides clearer information while keeping the screen less cluttered.
 Expanded Pause Menu
 Steam Cloud Save – Your save file, including all paint jobs, is now backed up to Steam, so you can continue your game on another computer.
 Improvements to Photo Mode – More polish and fixes to enhance the in-game photography experience.

Optimization & Performance

 Optimized the game to run better on more PC and Mac setups. Players on lower-end systems should see improved FPS and stability.
 New Downsampling Setting – Adjust graphics settings to improve performance without a major impact on visuals.
 Polished all weapons – Tweaks to make each weapon feel more satisfying to use.

Bug Fixes & Improvements

 Fixed “stuck on red loading screen” bug – This should no longer happen when loading into a world.
 Improvements to the Tutorial – Faster pacing and better guidance based on player feedback.
 General polish and bug fixes across multiple systems.

Join the Conversation!

If you enjoy the demo, please consider leaving a review on Steam and wishlisting the game—your support makes a huge difference! Also, join our Discord to share feedback, report bugs, and show off your best in-game photos!

Thanks for playing, and enjoy the update!

notes.title: Steam Achievements, Polish, and Bug Fixes
notes.notes:
Hey everyone!

This week, I’ve been focused on adding Steam achievements, polishing existing gameplay, and fixing reported bugs. As we get closer to release, my priority is making Wave Defense: Trappist feel stable, smooth, and satisfying to play.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45097607/97d61b0515dc8ed5527f1e33f35ba39b9ee11c04.png

Adding Steam Achievements

Achievements are a great way to give players a sense of progression and direction, rewarding them for key milestones while also encouraging them to experiment with different playstyles. Whether it’s exploring new worlds, mastering combat strategies, or simply capturing beautiful moments in Photo Mode, achievements will offer both recognition and subtle hints toward activities players may not have considered.

I want these to feel meaningful, not just like a checklist, so I’m carefully designing them to enhance the overall experience.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45097607/3973186e93dadca0f834ee7c0adb0a67b5ed1494.png

Polishing the Game vs. Adding More Features

Right now, I’m putting more effort into refining what’s already in the game rather than expanding systems or introducing new features. There’s a huge backlog of ideas I want to implement in future updates, but the focus at this stage is making sure that what’s in the game feels great to play.

Every mechanic, UI element, and interaction should feel intuitive, polished, and satisfying. The better the foundation, the more exciting it will be to expand on in the future.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45097607/ec3b850122f3a2819d78abbabc026bd211594342.png

Bug Fixes and Stability Improvements

With each patch, the game is becoming more stable and optimized. I’m prioritizing all reported bugs and issues I discover during testing. Every small fix contributes to a smoother experience, and it’s great to see the game running better with each update.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45097607/87ad3f3b09d6878caf2cc7ddd738eab5c3647a3b.png

Now’s the Time to Share Your Feedback!

If you have ideas, suggestions, or feedback, now is a great time to join our Discord and share your thoughts! As I continue to update the roadmap and backlog, community input is incredibly valuable in shaping the game’s future.

Thanks for your support—I can’t wait to share more soon! See you next Week.

Join the Discord!

Hello everyone! 

Rolling out a new update based on the feedback we’ve received from you. Your input has been instrumental in improving the game, so please keep it coming—either through the in-game feedback tool or by joining our Discord community! Here's what’s new in this update:

I hope these changes make your gameplay experience even better! As always, your feedback is invaluable—don’t hesitate to share your thoughts through in-game feedback or join our Discord community.

Thanks for playing, and see you in Wave Defense: Trappist!

notes.title: Demo Launch, New Features, and Bug Fixes
notes.notes:
Hey everyone!

What a week it’s been! The demo for Wave Defense: Trappist went live yesterday, and I couldn’t be happier with how things have turned out so far. This past week has been all about testing, stabilizing, and fixing bugs to ensure that the demo is the most feature-rich and stable version of the game yet.

Demo Launch and Early Feedback

It’s been a tough but rewarding week with plenty of late nights, but seeing the demo launch successfully has made it all worth it. So far, there haven’t been any reports of major bugs, which is a huge relief!

Even more exciting is the feedback and feature suggestions pouring in from players who are testing the demo. Some of the ideas coming in are fantastic, and it’s so exciting to see how engaged the community is becoming. Keep those suggestions coming!

The Discord channel is also growing steadily, which is wonderful to see. If you haven’t joined yet, this is the perfect time to do so. Share your thoughts, suggestions, and feedback—it’s the best way to help shape the game as it evolves toward its final release.

New Additions: Two Turrets and a Weapon

Alongside stabilizing the game, I’ve also added two new turrets and one new weapon to give players even more strategic options during battles. Here’s what’s new:

 Ionstrike Turret: A powerful long-range turret with a slow fire rate. It’s perfect for dealing massive damage from a distance, making it a great addition to your defense strategy.
 Tesla Coil Turret: The ultimate short-range turret with the highest rate of fire. It can’t reach far, but it’s amazing for taking out enemies that get too close to your base.

With these two new turrets, players can mix and match with the existing turret to create much more dynamic and personalized defenses.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45097607/4e6136ef308f4f82713e5b375178de8142708dbe.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45097607/af4863883cc933ceb309cada63c1b449ad9d9788.png
 Lazer Shotgun: A brand-new weapon for your mech, the Lazer Shotgun is an incredibly satisfying close-range powerhouse. It delivers a punch at short distances and is as fun to use as it is effective. I’m really looking forward to hearing what players think about it!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45097607/122c886de1813a21d4f7a4fc65c623816303d590.png
Looking Ahead

The next step is to keep gathering feedback and addressing any issues or suggestions as they come in. If you haven’t already, please consider leaving your thoughts in the Discord or through Steam. Your input during this demo phase is critical and will help shape the game for the better.

If you’re enjoying the demo, it would mean the world to me if you left a review on Steam and added the game to your wishlist. As a small indie developer, every bit of support makes a huge difference and helps the game reach more players.

Thank you so much for playing and being part of this journey—I can’t wait to see what you think of the new turrets, the shotgun, and the rest of the demo. See you in the Discord, and see you next week!

Join the Discord!
